description:
Programme or Project Overview

Maastricht University advertises a doctoral (promovendus) position on passende zorg in de wijkverpleging - appropriate care in Dutch district nursing. The project studies how quality, appropriateness and client-centredness of home nursing care are shaped in daily practice: which care decisions are made for which clients, how professional standards and real-world constraints interact, and how teams can improve fit between care delivered and care needed. The position is a salaried PhD employment under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement.

The candidate joins Maastricht University's health-services research environment, which combines qualitative and quantitative methods and works closely with care organisations in the region. Fieldwork runs in Dutch district nursing organisations, so professional working proficiency in Dutch is required for interviews and observations, while analysis and publication take place in English. The doctoral training runs through the university's graduate programme with a supervisory team spanning nursing science and health services research.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in nursing science, health sciences, health policy or a related discipline, with interest in care-organisation and workforce questions. Experience with qualitative methods, registry data or practice-oriented research is an advantage. Applications are submitted through Maastricht University's vacancy system; the closing date should be confirmed on the official vacancy page.

Highlights

  • Salaried PhD on appropriate care in district nursing
  • Maastricht University health-services research environment
  • Qualitative fieldwork in Dutch home-care organisations
  • Client-centred care quality and decision-making research
  • Dutch proficiency required for fieldwork
